review.tagline: Desktop app that builds apps from prompts on your own machine
review.summary: Dyad is a local, open-source prompt-to-app builder, positioned as an alternative to Lovable, v0 and Bolt that runs on your own computer. It ships as a downloadable app for Mac and Windows and uses your own AI API keys, with no sign-up. Code outside src/pro is Apache 2.0; src/pro is under the Functional Source License 1.1.
review.audience: Developers wanting a local Lovable/v0-style app builder with their own keys
strengths: Runs locally as a desktop app, with no sign-up needed to download
Bring your own API keys, so no hosted-platform lock-in
Code outside src/pro is Apache 2.0 licensed
weaknesses: src/pro is fair-source (FSL 1.1), not fully open-source
README does not list supported models or providers
No Linux build mentioned in the README
Desktop only; no Docker or self-hosted web deployment mentioned
needs: Needs Your own AI provider API keys
